audit_findings.title: Current-share denominator is paired with a stale debt-service numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed indication: $118 million pretax annualized interest increase versus FY2025, approximately $91 million after tax and $5.67 per share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025-derived OE anchor retains FY2025 interest expense while the share denominator reflects later repurchases and the company carries $49.718 billion of June 2026 debt.
audit_findings.evidence: Our average debt balance was $44.731 billion for 2025 compared to $41.388 billion for 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated. Annualizing first-half 2026 interest expense of $1.183 billion gives $2.366 billion, $118 million above FY2025. Applying the filed 23.0% first-half tax rate gives an indicative $91 million OE reduction. Because this could reduce BASE value from $419.17 to roughly $413.50 per share, it consumes about 57% of the $9.97 spread over the $409.20 market price and is reasonably capable of changing a marginal valuation conclusion after a complete run-rate reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile quarterly interest, average debt and debt issuance dates; calculate after-tax run-rate interest at June 30; identify debt-funded repurchases; replace the stale financing charge in anchor OE and rerun all scenarios and buy-below value.

audit_findings.title: Noncontrolling interests may contaminate parent-common owner earnings and cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scales are $998 million of 2025 NCI income, $827 million of 2025 NCI distributions and $1.013 billion of June 2026 consolidated cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with potentially consolidated D&A, capital expenditures, working-capital movements and bridge cash, although part of those consolidated resources belongs to noncontrolling owners.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, 2024 and 2023, we made distributions to noncontrolling interests of $827 million, $711 million and $640 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that controlled entities contain substantial minority claims, but it does not allocate the OE components or cash between HCA common shareholders and NCI. Excess consolidated D&A add-backs and cash would overstate value, while deducting consolidated capital spending attributable to NCI could understate it. The $998 million NCI income equals about 15% of the $6.656 billion anchor, so the unresolved claim mismatch is large enough to alter the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild each historical OE year from parent-attributable cash flows; allocate D&A, maintenance capex, working capital and cash by legal entity or ownership percentage; exclude restricted or NCI-owned cash; then recompute the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor is not visibly normalized for a known 2026 reimbursement decline
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scales include $6.2 billion of 2025 program revenue, approximately $400 million of Q2 2026 incremental net benefit and a computed $423 million pretax catch-up attributable to pre-2026 periods
audit_findings.mechanism: A change in recurring SDP reimbursement and Exchange-related uncompensated-care economics changes the sustainable OE starting level before scenario growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding the expected impact of any additional approvals, we expect revenues from SDP arrangements to decline in 2026 compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The lack of visible normalization is demonstrated, but the net direction and amount are unresolved. The original decline expectation was conditional on no additional approvals; Florida approval subsequently produced substantial benefit, including a nonrecurring $423 million pretax catch-up, while Exchange changes adversely affected managed-care revenue and first-half uncompensated-care cost increased $526 million year over year. These effects are individually large relative to the narrow $9.97 per-share BASE premium, so the sustainable starting level could change the conclusion even though the record does not establish the net adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Construct a 2026 run-rate OE bridge that removes the $423 million pre-2026 catch-up, separates recurring approved SDP economics from temporary approvals, quantifies EPTC and uncompensated-care effects, and rerun all scenarios from the normalized level.

audit_findings.title: Capital spending classified as growth may actually be required spending
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scales are $4.944 billion of FY2025 capex, a $5.0-$5.5 billion 2026 plan and $8.6 billion of June 2026 estimated project costs to complete
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required capital expenditure excluded as growth should reduce current OE; reinvestment necessary to produce projected growth must also be deducted from future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, there were projects under construction which had an estimated additional cost to complete and equip over the next five years of approximately $7.1 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: Misclassification is not yet demonstrated because the record does not identify which projects are maintenance, capacity-preserving or discretionary growth. Materiality is nevertheless established by scale: FY2025 capex was about 74% of the $6.656 billion anchor, and planned 2026 capex is about 75%-83% of it. Even a modest classification error could erase the BASE premium over market price or materially reduce the buy-below value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE maintenance-capex deduction to project-level actual and planned spending; classify compliance, replacement, technology, completion and capacity projects; link growth capex to scenario growth; and rerun the anchor and DCF with required reinvestment deducted.
